name: What countertops work best for an ADU kitchen used as a rental?

mainEntity.name: Which countertop materials are best for durability, maintenance, and resale in an ADU kitchen?
mainEntity.text: Which countertop materials are best for durability, maintenance, and resale in an ADU kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an ADU kitchen that will be used as a rental or guest unit, the best countertop is usually one that balances durability, easy maintenance, and visual appeal. Quartz is a common favorite because it resists stains well and gives a clean, high-end look without the maintenance concerns of some natural stones. Solid surface materials may also work if the project needs a simpler budget or a seamless appearance. Natural stone can look beautiful, but it may require more care and can be less forgiving in a small kitchen where every surface sees frequent use. The right choice also depends on how the kitchen is designed overall. Dark cabinets, light counters, and durable backsplash materials often create a polished result without overcomplicating the build. For Los Angeles-area ADUs, where many homeowners want both style and practicality, the best countertop is usually the one that keeps the kitchen looking good after years of use, not just on completion day.
acceptedAnswer.description: Quartz is often a strong choice for an ADU kitchen because it is durable, low maintenance, and consistent in appearance. Other materials may work, but the best countertop depends on budget, cooking habits, moisture exposure, and whether the unit will be rented or owner-occupied.
